proposals.code_does: The pool id is cached forever (src/lib.rs:52-62). After a different eviction policy is connected, ep.track(stale_pool,..).unwrap() at :101-103/:414/:598 panics with InvalidPool (eviction-policy-lru src/lib.rs:60-67) while state.inner is locked (:97/:409/:594). That poisons the mutex, so every later call panics. If the new policy already has that pool index, the entry is silently tracked in a foreign pool.
proposals.code_change: (1) Map track errors to DispatchMapError instead of unwrap() (in initialize, collect the first error from the for_each_extent closure). (2) Tie the cached pool id to the policy instance it came from (store the Arc and compare with Arc::ptr_eq, re-running create_pool on a mismatch), or forbid rebinding. (3) Add a reconnect-to-a-fresh-policy test that asserts Err rather than a panic and that the map still works afterwards.
proposals.alternative: BACKFILL FR-015: the eviction_policy receptacle MUST NOT be rebound after the first IDispatchMap call; still do step (1).
proposals.rationale: This was flagged on 2026-08-20 and 2026-10-13. Because the panic happens under the lock, the failure is permanent for the whole map.
